proof.criterion: Controller's relay: main's 'a route change that closes the issue moves the open card's route row without a reload', and whether the rewrite still proves the behaviour it named
proof.surface: the same rig, and main 5fbd8391 (git archive, its own Go server and bundle)
proof.command: main's recipients-claim.e2e.ts at the head (as a throwaway copy, deleted) and at main: `bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium e2e/recipients-claim.e2e.ts e2e/close-withdraws-asks.e2e.ts`
proof.observed: Main's version fails at main and at the head alike, at line 348: the moved route row never shows. #2233's close withdraws the open ask, and a withdrawn card lists no recipients, so a route row that moves in the same write as a close cannot be seen on either build. #2324 does not make main's version pass. The rewrite splits the write. A route change together with a status move (one issue.updated naming both) must move the open card's route row, and it does. The close that follows must withdraw the card ('Withdrawn when alice closed the issue') and leave no Recipients region, and it does. That is the reachable form of the behaviour the original test named.
proof.negativeControl: Main's version of the test at main itself: 1 failed (line 348), 9 passed in recipients-claim and close-withdraws-asks. Red on main, as the controller said.

proof.criterion: The rewritten in-flight Inbox claim test still proves 'a claim that lands while the Inbox is loading reaches the card that mounts from the earlier list'
proof.command: the branch's test (passed above), and main's version of it at the head (throwaway copy)
proof.observed: Main's version times out at the head (30 s). It holds the first Inbox load until a second Inbox request arrives, and that second request only comes when the first is cancelled; spec item 5 removes the cancel. The rewrite checks that the held body names no claimant (expect(staleClaimant).toBeNull()). It releases the body only after an event written after the claim has been handled, then requires the mounted card to list the claimant 'via claim'. It passes, so the behaviour named is still proven.
proof.negativeControl: Main's version at main passes, because main still cancels the first load. Its failure at head is the spec-mandated no-cancel behaviour, not a lost claim.

proof.criterion: #2233's withdrawal and restore: a close drops the issue's open asks from the person's Inbox tab and a reopen restores them, with no reload
proof.surface: the same rig; alice's Inbox and the issue page in two tabs, and a throwaway probe where another session (bob) closes and reopens while alice's Inbox is open
proof.command: close-withdraws-asks.e2e.ts in the run above; probe (deleted): bob PATCHes status done, then todo, while alice's Inbox shows the ask

An agent session's and the daemon's closes name the closer. Probe: the ask left alice's Inbox within 2 s of bob's close and returned within 2 s of his reopen (1 passed).
proof.negativeControl: The withdrawn decision shows no radio and no answer button, and the Inbox count for each ask id is 0 while closed, asserted by the test itself.
